claims.text: The header is written last but must not escape the budget, so its space is reserved up front.
claims.why: The claim references _HEADER_RESERVE which is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: A brief that overshoots by exactly the size of its own preamble is the kind of off-by-a-section that only shows up as a truncated prompt at the far end.
claims.why: The claim is about the overall behavior; the budget accounting is present but the preamble size is not defined here.

claims.text: Render a layer if it fits. Called in PRIORITY order, not display order.
claims.why: The docstring for _emit states priority order; the code calls _emit in order: imports, symbols, documents, which matches priority described.

claims.text: Priority matters because the layers are wildly different sizes: the 1-hop symbol layer around offload.py alone is 495 lines, and emitting it first consumed the entire budget and dropped the import layer -- the smallest and most valuable of the three, and the only one that answers 'what will I break'. Small high-value layers are rendered first and DISPLAYED in reading order.
claims.why: The code emits imports first (small, high-value), then symbols, then documents. The display order (symbols, imports, documents) is assembled later in sections list.

claims.text: Artefact importers are filtered HERE as well as in the neighbourhood.
claims.why: The code filters out artefact importers with _is_artefact on both outgoing and incoming edges.

claims.text: Measured: the first brief for shift.py had no artefact neighbour left and still printed '<- imported by runs/eval/deepseek_lab/wrecked/shift.py', because a reverse edge is read straight off the index and never passed through the walk.
claims.why: The code filters incoming edges with _is_artefact, addressing the issue described.

claims.text: PUBLIC API ONLY for a neighbour. What a caller may use from another module is its public surface; its private helpers are not callable and listing them cost 495 lines around offload.py -- enough to consume the whole budget on names nobody is allowed to reference.
claims.why: The code calls file_symbols with include_private=False for neighbours, limiting to public API.

claims.text: Both keys are absent unless the document layer is enabled, so this section vanishes rather than lying when it is off.
claims.why: The code checks include_docs and only builds doc_lines if True; otherwise the section is not emitted.

claims.text: A page that describes one of these files. Its claims are a PROMISE, not evidence -- where the code disagrees, the document is the bug.
claims.why: The docstring for the DOCUMENTS layer states this; the code emits the documents layer as described.

claims.text: DISPLAY order, independent of the priority order the layers were rendered in: symbols first because 'what exists' is what a writer needs before anything else, then who reaches whom, then what has been promised.
claims.why: The sections list is built with order ('symbols', 'imports', 'documents'), matching the described display order.

claims.text: If a name is not listed under its file, it does not exist in that file. Do not import it.
claims.why: The docstring for SYMBOLS THAT EXIST layer makes this claim; the code emits symbols that exist as determined by file_symbols.

claims.text: This describes SHAPE, not behaviour. Never cite it as evidence about what code does.
claims.why: The header includes this disclaimer; the code outputs it as part of the header.

observations.what: The _emit function uses nonlocal spent but does not account for the newline after head in the budget; head length may be off by 1 when note is empty (head = f'--- {title} ---\n').
_HEADER_RESERVE is referenced but not defined in this chunk; its value is unknown.

The dropped dictionary is set to len(lines) when no lines are kept, but if some lines are kept and later another layer overwrites dropped[layer]? Actually dropped[layer] is only set if kept < len(lines). That seems correct.
